name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
funding: Taipei City agency; 2025-26 sponsors incl. CTBC Culture & Education Fdn (bank), Chanel, Friends of TFAM, Winsing Arts Fdn, Luce Fdn.

name: Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB)
funding: State: run since 2018 by the Ministry of Culture's Taiwan Living Arts Foundation; budget figure not found.

name: TheCube Project Space
funding: The National Culture and Arts Foundation and the Department of Cultural Affairs of the Taipei City Government support it.

name: National Museum of Tajikistan
funding: No funder, budget or annual report found in the sources opened. Its official site did not load.

name: Dar Foto Festival
funding: Founded by Andrew Munuwa with Valentin Rudloff.

name: Nafasi Art Space
funding: Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC), Royal Norwegian Embassy, self-generated arts income; non-profit trust.

name: Bangkok Art Biennale
funding: BAB Foundation, chaired by ThaiBev CEO Thapana Sirivadhanabhakdi; ThaiBev is main partner, with Siam Piwat and Central Group (2018). Venice 2026 show adds Bangkok city, TAT, BEM, Ch. Karnchang, Generali.

name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
funding: ArtReview names the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration as its main funder. The administration said it would cut all funding from October 2017, fiscal year 2018.

name: Bangkok Kunsthalle
funding: Her husband Soopakij chairs CP Group, Thailand's largest private company.

name: Jim Thompson Art Center
funding: Run by the James H.W. Thompson Foundation, which says it relies entirely on its own funding.

name: MOCA Bangkok
funding: Privately owned by DTAC telecom founder Boonchai Bencharongkul, who built it in 2012 for his collection of over 1,000 works. His son Kanachai runs it; tickets cost THB 250.

name: MAIIAM
funding: Privately held by the Beurdeley-Bunnag family: Jean Michel Beurdeley, the late Patsri Bunnag and son Eric Bunnag Booth.
